laws.rule: Roatan Marine Park, the group that manages the Bay Islands National Marine Park around Roatan, lists these activities as prohibited in the park: fishing with nets or harpoons, taking lobster or conch, cutting mangroves, fishing herbivorous (plant-eating) fish species, anchoring on the reef, and construction. It lists as allowed: boat transit (speed cap 20 knots), use of anchor buoys, tourism, diving and snorkelling, artisanal handline fishing, lionfish hunting, research and education. The park has three zones: a coastal zone (high-tide line to 10 m depth), a special marine zone (to 60 m) and a buffer zone (12 nautical miles beyond). Its pages don't say which rule applies in which zone and don't name the legal instrument, so check with the park office.

local-law.notes: Only the Roatan section of the Bay Islands National Marine Park is covered. Utila and Guanaja park rules, and Honduran national and department rules, aren't checked here.

layers.authority: Roatan Marine Park (co-manager of the Bay Islands National Marine Park, Roatan)
layers.process: Roatan Marine Park asks visitors for a voluntary user fee of US$10 (about A$14.20 at A$1 = USD 0.7040, RBA 30 October 2026) to support reef conservation. It's described as voluntary, not a legal charge. Payers get a bracelet or token, sold at the park's EcoStore in West End or through participating dive shops and resorts.

zone-requirements.notes: Only Roatan Marine Park is covered. Any fee for Utila or Guanaja marine park areas, and any state-set fee for the Bay Islands, wasn't found.
